checks.note: It opens with "I'm so sorry your kettle arrived with a cracked lid again" and acknowledges the customer's frustration.
Refunds and money back are never mentioned, and nothing suggests one is coming. The draft goes straight to a replacement.
It offers a free replacement kettle with extra packing, and the customer doesn't have to return the damaged one.
The email is about 95 words, or about 103 with the subject line. Either way it's under 120.
The tone is warm. It notes this is the second time ("again") and mentions the four years of loyalty twice.

unasked_content: Mild friction: the draft makes the replacement depend on the customer sending a photo first ("If you could reply with a quick photo... I'll get the replacement shipped"). For a customer who is already angry and says they're 'done', that's an extra step, and it works a little against the friendly, make-it-right tone that was asked for.
